_about: Release 1 launch universe: the source of truth for stock_missions, stock_flags and the mission fields on stocks. Edit here, then run: node scripts/build-launch-seed.mjs

companies.mission_story: Develops medicines and vaccines, led by Keytruda, an immunotherapy that helps the immune system find and attack cancer.
companies.proof: Keytruda was the world's best-selling medicine in 2024, with about $29 billion in sales.
things_to_know: Keytruda's main U.S. patents begin expiring in 2028, a known challenge for Merck's growth.

missions.evidence: Oncology, led by Keytruda, is Merck's largest business.
missions.why_line: Its biggest medicine trains the immune system to fight cancer.

companies.mission_story: Develops medicines for cancer, blood disorders, immune diseases and heart disease, including the cancer immunotherapy Opdivo.
companies.proof: Opdivo is approved for many cancers, including lung, skin, kidney and bladder cancer.
things_to_know: Several top drugs, including Eliquis and Opdivo, face patent expirations later this decade.

missions.evidence: Oncology and blood cancers are among Bristol Myers Squibb's largest therapeutic areas.
missions.why_line: A large share of its medicines treat cancer.

companies.mission_story: One of the world's largest drugmakers, with medicines and vaccines for cancer, infections, heart disease and more.
companies.proof: Pfizer bought cancer-drug developer Seagen in 2023 for about $43 billion to expand its cancer medicines.
things_to_know: Sales of its COVID-19 products have fallen sharply since 2022.

missions.evidence: Oncology is one of Pfizer's main areas, expanded by the Seagen acquisition.
missions.why_line: Cancer is one of its biggest research areas, alongside vaccines.

companies.mission_story: Develops medicines for immune diseases, cancer and brain conditions, plus Botox through its Allergan business.
companies.proof: Its cancer drugs include Imbruvica and Venclexta, used to treat blood cancers such as leukemia.
things_to_know: Its former top seller, Humira, now faces lower-cost biosimilar competition.

missions.evidence: Oncology, including the blood-cancer drugs Imbruvica and Venclexta, is one of AbbVie's core areas.
missions.why_line: Part of its business develops treatments for blood cancers.

companies.mission_story: A biotechnology pioneer making medicines for cancer, bone loss, heart disease and inflammation.
companies.proof: Its cancer medicines include Kyprolis for multiple myeloma and Blincyto for leukemia.
things_to_know: Its 2023 purchase of Horizon Therapeutics added significant debt.

missions.evidence: Oncology and hematology are major therapeutic areas for Amgen.
missions.why_line: Several of its medicines treat blood cancers.

companies.mission_story: Discovers antibody medicines for eye disease, allergies, asthma and cancer, using its own genetic research tools.
companies.proof: Its Libtayo is an approved immunotherapy for certain skin and lung cancers.
things_to_know: Much of its income still depends on the eye drug Eylea, which faces new competition.

missions.evidence: Regeneron develops cancer immunotherapies, including Libtayo and several bispecific antibodies.
missions.why_line: It's building a growing set of cancer treatments.

companies.mission_story: Develops medicines for HIV, liver disease and cancer, including cell therapies that reprogram immune cells to fight cancer.
companies.proof: Its Kite unit makes the CAR T-cell therapies Yescarta and Tecartus for blood cancers.
things_to_know: Most of its sales still come from HIV medicines rather than cancer.

missions.evidence: Gilead's business is medicines for HIV, liver disease and cancer, including Kite's cell therapies.
missions.why_line: Its medicines treat HIV, and its Kite unit engineers immune cells to attack cancer.

companies.mission_story: Develops mRNA medicines and vaccines, including its COVID-19 vaccine, an RSV vaccine and experimental personalized cancer vaccines.
companies.proof: Its mRNA COVID-19 vaccine was one of the first two COVID-19 vaccines authorized in the U.S., in December 2020.
things_to_know: Not profitable since COVID-19 vaccine demand fell, and the stock is very volatile.

missions.evidence: Moderna's business is mRNA vaccines and therapies for infectious disease and cancer.
missions.why_line: Its whole platform is built on vaccines and treatments for disease.

companies.mission_story: A German biotech developing cancer immunotherapies and vaccines, best known for co-developing the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine.
companies.proof: It co-developed the first COVID-19 vaccine authorized in the U.S., in December 2020.
things_to_know: Results swing with vaccine demand, and it reports as a foreign company (Form 20-F).

missions.evidence: BioNTech's pipeline focuses on cancer immunotherapies and infectious-disease vaccines.
missions.why_line: It's betting its future on new ways to treat cancer.

companies.mission_story: Develops medicines that treat the root causes of serious diseases like cystic fibrosis and sickle cell disease.
companies.proof: Its Casgevy, approved in 2023, was the first approved CRISPR gene-editing therapy.
things_to_know: Most of its revenue still comes from cystic fibrosis medicines.

missions.evidence: Vertex develops medicines for cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease and other serious diseases.
missions.why_line: It focuses on treating the genetic causes of serious diseases.

companies.mission_story: Develops therapies for neurological diseases such as multiple sclerosis, spinal muscular atrophy and Alzheimer's disease.
companies.proof: It co-developed Leqembi, approved in 2023 as a treatment that slows early Alzheimer's disease.
things_to_know: Its older multiple sclerosis drugs face falling sales from generic competition.

missions.evidence: Biogen's business is medicines for neurological and neurodegenerative diseases.
missions.why_line: It works on hard-to-treat brain diseases like Alzheimer's.

companies.mission_story: Makes tools used to research diseases, manufacture biologic medicines and diagnose patients, through brands like Cytiva, Beckman Coulter and Cepheid.
companies.proof: Its Cepheid GeneXpert systems are used worldwide to diagnose tuberculosis and other infections.
things_to_know: Demand for its tools slowed after the COVID-19 testing boom ended.

missions.evidence: Danaher's diagnostics and life-science tools support disease testing and drug development.
missions.why_line: Its tests and lab tools help diagnose disease and develop new treatments.

companies.mission_story: Develops blood tests that find cancer and help doctors choose treatments, without needing a tissue biopsy.
companies.proof: Its Shield test became the first FDA-approved blood test for primary colorectal cancer screening, in 2024.
things_to_know: Not yet profitable; growth depends on doctors and insurers adopting its tests.

missions.evidence: Guardant Health's business is blood-based cancer detection and monitoring tests.
missions.why_line: Its blood tests aim to catch cancer earlier and guide treatment.

profile.description: Guardant Health develops blood tests that detect cancer and guide treatment, including Guardant360 for advanced cancer and the Shield colorectal cancer screening test.

companies.mission_story: Develops genetic blood tests that check whether cancer has returned, screen pregnancies and monitor transplanted organs.
companies.proof: Its Signatera test is personalized to each patient's tumor to detect cancer recurrence from a blood draw.
things_to_know: Has a history of losses while investing heavily in growth.

missions.evidence: Natera's cell-free DNA tests are used to detect cancer recurrence and screen for genetic conditions.
missions.why_line: Its blood tests help catch cancer coming back earlier.

profile.description: Natera develops cell-free DNA tests for cancer monitoring, prenatal screening and organ transplant health.

companies.mission_story: Makes the DNA sequencing machines labs use to read genes, study cancer and diagnose genetic disease.
companies.proof: Its technology helped cut the cost of sequencing a human genome from millions of dollars to a few hundred.
things_to_know: Spun off the cancer-test maker Grail in 2024 after regulators challenged the acquisition.

missions.evidence: Illumina's sequencing is used in cancer research and genetic disease diagnosis.
missions.why_line: Its machines power much of the genetic research behind new cancer tests.

profile.description: Illumina makes DNA sequencing machines and chemistry used in genetic research, cancer testing and disease diagnosis.

companies.mission_story: Develops medicines for blood cancers, other cancers and inflammatory skin conditions.
companies.proof: Its drug Jakafi treats myelofibrosis and polycythemia vera, two rare blood cancers.
things_to_know: Jakafi, its main drug, loses U.S. patent protection later this decade.

missions.evidence: Incyte's main medicines treat blood cancers and other cancers.
missions.why_line: Most of its work goes into new cancer medicines.

profile.description: Incyte discovers and develops medicines for cancer and inflammatory diseases, led by Jakafi for rare blood cancers.

companies.mission_story: A focused cancer-drug company whose main medicine treats kidney, liver and thyroid cancers.
companies.proof: Its drug Cabometyx is approved for advanced kidney cancer, liver cancer and certain thyroid cancers.
things_to_know: Depends heavily on a single drug, Cabometyx.

missions.evidence: Exelixis's business is discovering and selling cancer medicines.
missions.why_line: Cancer is the entire focus of the company.

profile.description: Exelixis develops cancer medicines, led by Cabometyx for kidney, liver and thyroid cancers.

companies.mission_story: Pioneered medicines that switch off disease-causing genes, starting with rare inherited diseases and expanding into heart disease.
companies.proof: Its Onpattro, approved in 2018, was the first FDA-approved RNAi medicine.
things_to_know: Has spent heavily on research, and its profits depend on a few key medicines.

missions.evidence: Alnylam develops RNAi medicines for genetic and cardiometabolic diseases.
missions.why_line: It treats diseases by silencing the genes that cause them.

profile.description: Alnylam develops RNA interference (RNAi) medicines that silence disease-causing genes, for rare and common diseases.

companies.mission_story: Develops medicines for rare genetic diseases that often have few or no other treatments.
companies.proof: Its Voxzogo was the first approved medicine to increase growth in children with achondroplasia, the most common form of dwarfism.
things_to_know: Rare-disease medicines serve small patient groups, so each launch matters a lot.

missions.evidence: BioMarin focuses on medicines for rare genetic diseases.
missions.why_line: It focuses on rare diseases that often have no other treatment.

profile.description: BioMarin develops medicines for rare genetic diseases, including enzyme therapies and a treatment for achondroplasia.

companies.mission_story: Makes the kits and tests labs use to extract and analyze DNA, including tests for tuberculosis, infections and cancer markers.
companies.proof: Its QuantiFERON test is widely used to screen for latent tuberculosis infection.
things_to_know: Incorporated in the Netherlands, so results are sensitive to currency moves.

missions.evidence: Qiagen's molecular diagnostics are used to detect infectious diseases and cancer biomarkers.
missions.why_line: Its tests help labs detect disease and guide cancer treatment.

profile.description: Qiagen makes sample-preparation kits and molecular tests used by labs to detect infections, cancer markers and genetic conditions.

companies.mission_story: Makes medical devices, diagnostic tests, nutrition products and medicines, including the FreeStyle Libre glucose monitor.
companies.proof: Its FreeStyle Libre glucose monitors are used by millions of people with diabetes worldwide.
things_to_know: Faces lawsuits over formula products for premature infants.

missions.evidence: Abbott's medical devices, including diabetes care and heart devices, are its fastest-growing business.
missions.why_line: Its glucose monitors help people manage diabetes day to day.

companies.mission_story: Makes continuous glucose monitors that let people with diabetes track their blood sugar in real time without finger pricks.
companies.proof: In 2024 it launched Stelo, the first over-the-counter glucose biosensor cleared by the FDA.
things_to_know: Faces strong competition from Abbott's FreeStyle Libre.

missions.evidence: Dexcom's entire business is continuous glucose monitoring.
missions.why_line: Its sensors help people with diabetes avoid dangerous blood-sugar swings.

companies.mission_story: Makes the Omnipod, a small tubeless insulin pump worn on the body, for people with diabetes.
companies.proof: Omnipod 5 works with continuous glucose monitors to adjust insulin delivery automatically.
things_to_know: Competes with larger device makers and newer diabetes medicines.

missions.evidence: Insulet's business is the Omnipod insulin delivery system.
missions.why_line: Its pump makes managing insulin simpler for people with diabetes.

profile.description: Insulet makes the Omnipod, a tubeless, wearable insulin pump for people with diabetes.

companies.mission_story: Makes the da Vinci robotic surgery system, which helps surgeons perform minimally invasive operations.
companies.proof: Surgeons have performed millions of procedures with da Vinci systems since its first FDA clearance in 2000.
things_to_know: The stock is valued at a high multiple of earnings.

missions.evidence: Intuitive's da Vinci systems enable minimally invasive surgery, which typically means smaller incisions and faster recovery.
missions.why_line: Its robots help patients recover faster from surgery.

companies.mission_story: Makes heart valves and devices that let doctors replace or repair heart valves without open-heart surgery.
companies.proof: It pioneered transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), which replaces a heart valve through a catheter.
things_to_know: Sold its critical care business in 2024 to focus on structural heart devices.

missions.evidence: Edwards focuses on devices for structural heart disease.
missions.why_line: Its valves give heart patients an option without open-heart surgery.

companies.mission_story: Makes devices for heart, vascular, digestive and urological conditions, including treatments for irregular heartbeat.
companies.proof: Its Farapulse system uses pulsed electric fields to treat atrial fibrillation, a common irregular heartbeat.
things_to_know: Has grown through many acquisitions, which carry integration risk.

missions.evidence: Boston Scientific makes medical devices for cardiology, vascular and other conditions.
missions.why_line: Its devices treat heart conditions with less invasive procedures.

companies.mission_story: One of the largest medical device companies, making pacemakers, insulin pumps, spine and surgical tools.
companies.proof: Its Micra is a leadless pacemaker small enough to be placed directly in the heart through a vein.
things_to_know: Growth has been slower than at smaller device makers.

missions.evidence: Medtronic's devices treat heart rhythm, diabetes, spine and neurological conditions.
missions.why_line: Its devices keep hearts beating in rhythm and help manage chronic disease.

companies.mission_story: Makes orthopedic implants, surgical equipment and robotic systems for joint replacement.
companies.proof: Its Mako robotic-arm system assists surgeons with knee and hip replacements.
things_to_know: Hospital spending cycles can affect equipment sales.

missions.evidence: Stryker makes medical technology for orthopedics, surgery and neurotechnology.
missions.why_line: Its implants and robots help people stay mobile after joint damage.

companies.mission_story: Makes knee and hip replacement implants and related surgical technology.
companies.proof: It is one of the largest makers of knee and hip replacement implants.
things_to_know: Its growth has lagged rivals, and it has faced product recalls.

missions.evidence: Zimmer Biomet focuses on joint reconstruction implants.
missions.why_line: Its replacement joints help people walk without pain.

companies.mission_story: Makes CPAP machines and masks that treat sleep apnea, plus cloud software that tracks patients' therapy.
companies.proof: Its AirSense devices connect to the cloud so care teams can see how patients are using their therapy.
things_to_know: Weight-loss drugs could reduce sleep apnea cases over time, a debated risk to its sales.

missions.evidence: ResMed's business is devices and software for sleep apnea and respiratory care.
missions.why_line: Treating sleep apnea lowers the risk of heart disease and constant fatigue.

profile.description: ResMed makes CPAP machines, masks and software for sleep apnea and other breathing disorders.

companies.mission_story: Makes a small implant that treats sleep apnea by keeping the airway open during sleep, for people who can't tolerate CPAP.
companies.proof: Its therapy works by stimulating the nerve that moves the tongue, keeping the airway open during sleep.
things_to_know: Weight-loss drugs and competing devices are watched closely as risks to growth.

missions.evidence: Inspire's business is its implanted sleep apnea therapy.
missions.why_line: It offers sleep apnea relief for people who can't use a mask.

profile.description: Inspire Medical Systems makes an implanted device that treats obstructive sleep apnea for people who can't use CPAP.

companies.mission_story: Makes Zio, a wearable patch that records heart rhythms for up to two weeks to help detect conditions like atrial fibrillation.
companies.proof: Its Zio patch is worn for up to 14 days, and the recordings are analyzed with AI-assisted software.
things_to_know: Not yet consistently profitable and depends on insurance reimbursement rates.

missions.evidence: iRhythm's business is wearable heart-rhythm monitoring.
missions.why_line: Catching irregular heartbeats early can help prevent strokes.

profile.description: iRhythm Technologies makes the Zio wearable heart monitor and analysis service to detect irregular heart rhythms.

companies.mission_story: Makes devices that remove blood clots from arteries and veins, used to treat strokes and blood clots in the lungs.
companies.proof: Its computer-assisted vacuum devices pull clots out through a thin catheter.
things_to_know: Competition in clot-removal devices is increasing.

missions.evidence: Penumbra's devices treat strokes and vascular blockages.
missions.why_line: Its devices help stroke and clot patients recover with less damage.

profile.description: Penumbra makes devices that remove blood clots, used to treat strokes, pulmonary embolisms and other vascular conditions.

companies.mission_story: Develops tiny implants and drug-delivery treatments for glaucoma and other chronic eye diseases.
companies.proof: Its iStent is among the smallest medical devices ever approved by the FDA.
things_to_know: Not consistently profitable, and new products depend on insurance coverage decisions.

missions.evidence: Glaukos focuses on glaucoma and corneal disease treatments.
missions.why_line: Its implants help protect people's eyesight from glaucoma.

profile.description: Glaukos develops treatments for glaucoma and other eye diseases, including tiny stents implanted during eye surgery.

companies.mission_story: Keeps donor hearts, lungs and livers warm and functioning outside the body, and flies them to transplant centers.
companies.proof: Its Organ Care System keeps donor organs perfused and working during transport instead of packing them on ice.
things_to_know: A volatile stock; growth depends on transplant volumes and its aviation logistics.

missions.evidence: TransMedics' business is organ preservation and transplant logistics.
missions.why_line: It helps more donor organs reach the patients who need them.

profile.description: TransMedics makes the Organ Care System, which keeps donor organs functioning outside the body, and runs an aviation network to transport them.

companies.mission_story: Helps hospitals and device makers prevent infections with sterilization equipment, services and supplies.
companies.proof: It sterilizes medical devices for manufacturers and surgical instruments for hospitals.
things_to_know: A steady but slower-growing business tied to hospital procedure volumes.

missions.evidence: Steris's products and services reduce infection risk in healthcare.
missions.why_line: Its sterilization keeps surgeries and hospitals safer.

profile.description: Steris provides sterilization equipment, services and products that help hospitals and medical device makers prevent infections.

companies.mission_story: Runs one of the largest networks of medical testing labs, used for checkups, disease screening and diagnosis.
companies.proof: Quest says it serves about one in three U.S. adults each year.
things_to_know: Lab testing prices are pressured by insurers and government reimbursement rules.

missions.evidence: Quest's diagnostic testing supports disease screening and preventive care.
missions.why_line: Routine lab tests help catch health problems early.

profile.description: Quest Diagnostics runs clinical laboratories that perform medical tests for doctors, hospitals, employers and consumers.

companies.mission_story: Runs medical testing labs used by doctors and patients, and supports the development of new medicines.
companies.proof: Labcorp processes hundreds of millions of lab tests each year.
things_to_know: Spun off its clinical-trials business, Fortrea, in 2023.

missions.evidence: Labcorp's diagnostics support disease detection and prevention.
missions.why_line: Its lab tests help doctors catch problems early.

profile.description: Labcorp runs clinical laboratories for medical testing and provides lab services for drug development.

companies.mission_story: Develops medicines for diabetes, obesity, cancer, immune diseases and Alzheimer's disease.
companies.proof: Its tirzepatide is sold as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for weight loss.
things_to_know: Its stock price assumes strong long-term growth from obesity medicines.

missions.evidence: Diabetes and obesity medicines are Lilly's largest and fastest-growing business.
missions.why_line: Its medicines help people manage diabetes and lose weight.

missions.evidence: Lilly's oncology medicines include Verzenio for breast cancer.
missions.why_line: It also develops cancer medicines, such as Verzenio for breast cancer.

companies.mission_story: A Danish drugmaker focused on diabetes and obesity, the maker of insulin, Ozempic and Wegovy.
companies.proof: Novo Nordisk has made insulin since the 1920s.
things_to_know: Faces intense competition from Eli Lilly in obesity medicines, and reports as a foreign company (Form 20-F).

missions.evidence: Novo Nordisk's business centers on diabetes and obesity care.
missions.why_line: Its medicines help millions of people manage diabetes and weight.

profile.description: Novo Nordisk develops diabetes and obesity medicines, including Ozempic and Wegovy, and treatments for rare blood disorders.

companies.mission_story: Owns Florida's largest electric utility and one of the world's largest developers of wind and solar power.
companies.proof: Its NextEra Energy Resources unit is one of the world's largest generators of power from wind and sun.
things_to_know: Its Florida utility still generates much of its power from natural gas.

missions.evidence: NextEra develops and operates large wind, solar and battery storage projects.
missions.why_line: It builds more wind and solar power than almost anyone.

flags.evidence: Florida Power & Light generates a large share of its electricity from natural gas.

companies.mission_story: Makes thin-film solar panels using a different technology from most rivals, with large factories in the United States.
companies.proof: It is the largest U.S.-based solar panel manufacturer.
things_to_know: Its profits depend partly on U.S. clean-energy tax credits.

missions.evidence: First Solar's business is manufacturing solar modules.
missions.why_line: Every panel it makes adds clean power to the grid.

profile.description: First Solar makes thin-film solar panels, with factories in the United States and Asia.

companies.mission_story: Makes microinverters and home batteries that turn rooftop solar into usable electricity and store it.
companies.proof: It pioneered microinverters, which convert power at each solar panel instead of at one central inverter.
things_to_know: Home solar demand has fallen with higher interest rates, and the stock is volatile.

missions.evidence: Enphase's products are used in residential and commercial solar systems.
missions.why_line: It helps households generate and store their own clean power.

profile.description: Enphase Energy makes microinverters, batteries and software for home solar systems.

companies.mission_story: Makes solar trackers that tilt panels to follow the sun, helping large solar farms produce more power.
companies.proof: It has been one of the world's largest solar tracker suppliers by shipments for years.
things_to_know: Renamed from Nextracker to Nextpower; demand depends on large solar project timelines.

missions.evidence: Nextpower's business is equipment for utility-scale solar plants.
missions.why_line: Its trackers get more clean electricity out of every solar farm.

profile.description: Nextpower (formerly Nextracker) makes solar trackers, which tilt solar panels to follow the sun, plus other solar power-plant equipment.

companies.mission_story: Makes trackers that move solar panels to follow the sun at large solar power plants.
companies.proof: It has been building solar tracking systems since 1989.
things_to_know: Smaller and more volatile than its main rival, Nextpower.

missions.evidence: Array's business is solar tracking systems.
missions.why_line: It helps large solar farms produce more clean power.

profile.description: Array Technologies makes solar trackers and related equipment for utility-scale solar projects.

companies.mission_story: Makes fuel-cell power systems that generate electricity on-site with lower emissions than burning fuel.
companies.proof: Its fuel cells produce electricity through an electrochemical reaction rather than combustion.
things_to_know: Most of its systems currently run on natural gas, though they can use hydrogen.

missions.evidence: Bloom's fuel cells provide lower-emission on-site power and can run on hydrogen.
missions.why_line: It offers cleaner on-site power than traditional generators.

flags.evidence: Most Bloom fuel cells currently run on natural gas.

profile.description: Bloom Energy makes solid-oxide fuel cells that generate electricity on-site, including for data centers.

companies.mission_story: Builds large battery systems that store electricity for the grid, making wind and solar power more reliable.
companies.proof: It was formed in 2018 by Siemens and AES, two longtime energy companies.
things_to_know: Margins are thin, and the stock is volatile.

missions.evidence: Fluence's business is grid-scale energy storage.
missions.why_line: Batteries let solar and wind power keep flowing after the sun sets.

profile.description: Fluence Energy provides battery energy storage systems and software for power grids.

companies.mission_story: Operates the largest fleet of nuclear power plants in the U.S., the country's biggest source of carbon-free electricity.
companies.proof: It is the largest producer of carbon-free energy in the United States.
things_to_know: Also owns natural gas power plants, and nuclear power is controversial to some.

missions.evidence: Most of Constellation's power comes from nuclear plants, which emit no carbon.
missions.why_line: Its nuclear plants produce huge amounts of carbon-free power.

flags.evidence: Constellation also operates natural gas power plants.

profile.description: Constellation Energy is the largest U.S. producer of nuclear power and sells electricity to businesses and homes.

companies.mission_story: Owns one of the world's largest portfolios of renewable power, from hydroelectric dams to wind and solar farms.
companies.proof: In 2024 it agreed to supply Microsoft with more than 10.5 gigawatts of new renewable power.
things_to_know: A limited partnership that reports as a foreign company (Form 20-F); its distributions are taxed differently.

missions.evidence: Brookfield Renewable's business is owning and operating renewable power assets.
missions.why_line: Its dams, wind and solar farms run on renewable power.

profile.description: Brookfield Renewable owns and operates hydroelectric, wind, solar and storage facilities around the world.

companies.mission_story: Owns wind, solar and battery projects across the U.S. and pays out much of its cash flow as dividends.
companies.proof: It sells most of its power under long-term contracts with utilities and companies.
things_to_know: Also owns some natural gas plants and carries significant debt.

missions.evidence: Most of Clearway's generating capacity is wind and solar.
missions.why_line: Its farms generate renewable power under long-term contracts.

flags.evidence: Clearway owns natural gas generating facilities alongside its renewables.

profile.description: Clearway Energy owns wind, solar and battery storage projects across the U.S. and sells their power under long-term contracts.

companies.mission_story: Generates electricity from the Earth's heat, one of the few renewable sources that runs around the clock.
companies.proof: It has been developing geothermal power technology since the 1960s.
things_to_know: Geothermal projects take years to develop and are capital-intensive.

missions.evidence: Ormat's main business is geothermal power generation.
missions.why_line: Its plants make clean power day and night from underground heat.

profile.description: Ormat Technologies develops and operates geothermal power plants and makes geothermal and energy storage equipment.

companies.mission_story: Invests in and lends to clean energy and climate projects, from solar and wind to energy efficiency.
companies.proof: It reports the carbon emissions its investments avoid each year, using a metric it calls CarbonCount.
things_to_know: A financial company whose results are sensitive to interest rates.

missions.evidence: HASI's business is financing climate-positive infrastructure.
missions.why_line: It funds the projects that cut carbon emissions.

profile.description: HA Sustainable Infrastructure Capital invests in climate solutions such as renewable energy, energy efficiency and sustainable infrastructure.

companies.mission_story: The largest U.S. home solar company, installing rooftop solar and batteries that households lease or buy.
companies.proof: It is the largest residential solar installer in the United States.
things_to_know: Carries a lot of debt and depends on tax credits; the stock is very volatile.

missions.evidence: Sunrun's business is residential solar and battery systems.
missions.why_line: It puts solar panels and batteries on people's homes.

profile.description: Sunrun installs and finances rooftop solar and home battery systems for households.

companies.mission_story: Makes electric vehicles, home and grid batteries, and solar products, and is developing self-driving technology.
companies.proof: Its Megapack batteries store electricity at grid scale, and energy storage is one of its fastest-growing businesses.
things_to_know: Valued like a tech company; the stock is very volatile and closely tied to its CEO.

missions.evidence: Tesla's business is electric vehicles and energy storage.
missions.why_line: Its cars and batteries help move transport and power away from fossil fuels.

companies.mission_story: Builds wind turbines and the grid equipment that carries power, and services a large share of the world's power plants.
companies.proof: It was spun off from General Electric in 2024 as GE's energy business.
things_to_know: A large part of its business is gas turbines for fossil-fuel power plants.

missions.evidence: GE Vernova's wind and electrification businesses support renewable power and grid upgrades.
missions.why_line: Its wind turbines and grid equipment help connect clean power.

flags.evidence: GE Vernova makes gas turbines for power plants.

profile.description: GE Vernova makes wind turbines, grid equipment and gas turbines, and services power plants worldwide.

companies.mission_story: Makes electrical equipment that manages power in buildings, data centers and grids, helping electrify the economy.
companies.proof: Its products include equipment that connects solar, batteries and EV chargers to buildings and the grid.
things_to_know: Much of its demand comes from data centers and industry, not only clean energy.

missions.evidence: Eaton's electrical business supports electrification and energy efficiency.
missions.why_line: Its equipment helps buildings and grids use power more efficiently.

profile.description: Eaton is a power management company making electrical equipment for buildings, utilities, data centers, vehicles and aircraft.

companies.mission_story: A global power company shifting toward wind, solar and batteries, and a major supplier of clean power to tech companies.
companies.proof: It has signed long-term clean-power contracts with large tech companies, including Google and Microsoft.
things_to_know: Still operates coal and gas plants and carries significant debt.

missions.evidence: AES is building large amounts of renewable generation and battery storage.
missions.why_line: It's moving its power business toward wind, solar and batteries.

flags.evidence: AES operates coal and natural gas power plants.

profile.description: AES is a global power company developing renewable energy and battery storage and operating utilities.

companies.mission_story: A utility serving eight states and one of the largest providers of wind power among U.S. utilities.
companies.proof: In 2018 it became the first major U.S. utility to commit to 100% carbon-free electricity by 2050.
things_to_know: Still burns coal and natural gas for part of its power.

missions.evidence: Xcel generates a large share of its electricity from wind and plans to retire its coal plants.
missions.why_line: It's one of the utilities pushing hardest toward carbon-free power.

flags.evidence: Xcel still generates part of its electricity from coal and natural gas.

companies.mission_story: A large utility serving 11 states and the owner of one of the largest U.S. electricity transmission networks.
companies.proof: It operates the largest electricity transmission system in the United States.
things_to_know: Coal and natural gas still make up a large share of its generation.

missions.evidence: AEP is investing in transmission and renewable generation to modernize the grid.
missions.why_line: Its transmission lines move power, including renewables, across the grid.

flags.evidence: AEP generates a large share of its electricity from coal and natural gas.

companies.mission_story: One of the world's largest lithium producers, supplying a key material for electric-vehicle and grid batteries.
companies.proof: It produces lithium from brine in Chile and from hard-rock mines in Australia.
things_to_know: Lithium prices swing widely, making profits and the stock volatile.

missions.evidence: Albemarle's lithium is used in batteries for EVs and energy storage.
missions.why_line: Its lithium goes into the batteries behind EVs and clean power.

profile.description: Albemarle is one of the world's largest lithium producers, supplying battery materials, plus bromine and refining catalysts.

companies.mission_story: Protects computers, cloud systems and user identities from cyberattacks with its Falcon platform.
companies.proof: Its Falcon platform uses a single lightweight agent on each device to detect and stop attacks.
things_to_know: A faulty software update in July 2024 crashed millions of Windows computers worldwide.

missions.evidence: CrowdStrike's business is cybersecurity.
missions.why_line: It stops hackers before they can break in.

companies.mission_story: One of the largest cybersecurity companies, protecting networks, cloud systems and security operations.
companies.proof: Its customers include most of the Fortune 100.
things_to_know: Agreed in 2025 to buy CyberArk, its largest acquisition.

missions.evidence: Palo Alto Networks' business is cybersecurity.
missions.why_line: It defends companies and governments against cyberattacks.

companies.mission_story: Makes firewalls and network security systems that protect businesses from cyberattacks.
companies.proof: It designs its own security chips to speed up its firewalls.
things_to_know: Sales depend partly on hardware upgrade cycles.

missions.evidence: Fortinet's business is network security.
missions.why_line: Its firewalls keep attackers out of business networks.

companies.mission_story: Provides cloud-based security that connects employees to apps safely without a traditional company network.
companies.proof: Its cloud processes hundreds of billions of transactions a day.
things_to_know: Not consistently profitable under standard accounting.

missions.evidence: Zscaler's business is cloud-delivered security.
missions.why_line: It protects people working from anywhere.

companies.mission_story: Runs a global network that protects websites and apps from attacks and makes them faster.
companies.proof: Its network runs in more than 300 cities worldwide.
things_to_know: Highly valued relative to its current profits.

missions.evidence: Cloudflare's network provides security services such as DDoS protection and zero-trust access.
missions.why_line: It shields websites from attacks that would knock them offline.

companies.mission_story: Provides identity software that controls who can sign in to apps and systems.
companies.proof: It offers identity tools for both employees and customers, including the Auth0 platform.
things_to_know: Suffered a security breach of its customer support system in 2023.

missions.evidence: Okta's business is identity and access security.
missions.why_line: It makes sure only the right people can get into accounts.

companies.mission_story: Uses AI to detect and stop cyberattacks on computers, cloud systems and identities automatically.
companies.proof: Its platform can roll a Windows device back to its state before a ransomware attack.
things_to_know: Not yet profitable, and it competes with much larger rivals.

missions.evidence: SentinelOne's business is cybersecurity.
missions.why_line: Its AI stops attacks automatically, even before people notice.

profile.description: SentinelOne provides AI-powered cybersecurity that protects devices, cloud workloads and identities.

companies.mission_story: One of the original cybersecurity companies, protecting networks, cloud systems and email from attacks.
companies.proof: It helped pioneer the commercial firewall in the 1990s.
things_to_know: Grows more slowly than newer rivals, and reports as a foreign company (Form 20-F).

missions.evidence: Check Point's business is cybersecurity.
missions.why_line: It has been protecting networks from attacks for decades.

profile.description: Check Point Software provides firewalls, cloud security and threat prevention to businesses and governments.

companies.mission_story: Finds security weaknesses in computer systems before attackers can exploit them.
companies.proof: It created Nessus, one of the most widely used vulnerability scanners.
things_to_know: Competes in a crowded security market.

missions.evidence: Tenable's business is vulnerability and exposure management.
missions.why_line: It finds the holes before hackers do.

profile.description: Tenable makes exposure-management software that finds security weaknesses across IT systems.

companies.mission_story: Helps security teams find weak spots and detect attacks across their systems.
companies.proof: It maintains Metasploit, a widely used open-source tool for testing security.
things_to_know: Faces tough competition and slowing growth.

missions.evidence: Rapid7's business is security operations and vulnerability management.
missions.why_line: It helps security teams spot attacks early.

profile.description: Rapid7 provides security operations and vulnerability management software for businesses.

companies.mission_story: Scans companies' computers and cloud systems for security weaknesses and compliance gaps.
companies.proof: It was one of the first companies to deliver security scanning as a cloud service.
things_to_know: A smaller company facing larger, faster-growing competitors.

missions.evidence: Qualys's business is cloud-based security and compliance.
missions.why_line: It continuously checks systems for weaknesses attackers could use.

profile.description: Qualys provides cloud-based IT security and compliance software.

companies.mission_story: Protects sensitive data by finding where it lives, who can access it, and spotting suspicious activity.
companies.proof: It focuses on protecting data itself, such as files and email, rather than the network around it.
things_to_know: It is moving customers to a cloud subscription model, which affects reported results.

missions.evidence: Varonis's business is data security.
missions.why_line: It keeps sensitive files and emails out of the wrong hands.

profile.description: Varonis makes data security software that finds sensitive data and detects threats to it.

companies.mission_story: Protects companies' data with backups that attackers can't change, helping them recover from ransomware.
companies.proof: Its backups are designed to be immutable, so ransomware can't alter or delete them.
things_to_know: Not yet profitable.

missions.evidence: Rubrik's business is data security and cyber recovery.
missions.why_line: It helps organizations bounce back after ransomware.

profile.description: Rubrik provides data security and backup software that helps organizations recover from ransomware attacks.

companies.mission_story: Makes Norton, Avast and LifeLock, protecting everyday people from viruses, scams and identity theft.
companies.proof: It says its products protect around 500 million users worldwide.
things_to_know: Carries significant debt from its Avast acquisition.

missions.evidence: Gen Digital's business is consumer cyber safety.
missions.why_line: It protects regular people from scams and identity theft.

profile.description: Gen Digital makes consumer cybersecurity and privacy products, including Norton, Avast and LifeLock.

companies.mission_story: Runs one of the world's largest networks for delivering websites and protecting them from attacks.
companies.proof: Security has become its largest business, ahead of content delivery.
things_to_know: Its original content-delivery business is shrinking.

missions.evidence: Akamai's security services protect websites, apps and APIs from attacks.
missions.why_line: It shields major websites from attacks that would take them down.

profile.description: Akamai runs a large content delivery and cloud network and sells cybersecurity services that protect websites and apps.

companies.mission_story: The largest maker of networking equipment, with a growing security business that includes Splunk.
companies.proof: It bought Splunk in 2024 for about $28 billion, expanding its security business.
things_to_know: Security is still a minority of Cisco's revenue.

missions.evidence: Cisco's security products, including Splunk, protect networks and detect threats.
missions.why_line: Part of its business protects the networks it builds.

companies.mission_story: Makes safety gear that protects firefighters and workers, from breathing equipment to gas detectors and hard hats.
companies.proof: It was founded in 1914 to make safety equipment for coal miners.
things_to_know: Sales depend on industrial and fire-department budgets.

missions.evidence: MSA's business is safety equipment for workers and first responders.
missions.why_line: Its gear helps firefighters and workers come home safe.

profile.description: MSA Safety makes safety equipment such as gas detectors, firefighter breathing gear and hard hats.

companies.mission_story: Provides home security systems and 24/7 alarm monitoring for homes and businesses.
companies.proof: It has provided security services for more than 150 years.
things_to_know: Carries a lot of debt.

missions.evidence: ADT's business is security monitoring for homes and businesses.
missions.why_line: It watches over homes around the clock.

profile.description: ADT provides home security and monitoring services, including alarms, cameras and smart-home devices.

companies.mission_story: Makes locks and access systems, including Schlage, that secure homes, schools and businesses.
companies.proof: It owns Schlage, a lock brand founded in 1920.
things_to_know: Tied to construction and renovation activity.

missions.evidence: Allegion's locks and access systems secure buildings.
missions.why_line: Its locks keep homes, schools and businesses secure.

profile.description: Allegion makes locks, door hardware and access-control systems, including the Schlage brand.

companies.mission_story: Makes body cameras, evidence software and TASER devices for police, with a stated goal of making the bullet obsolete.
companies.proof: Its body cameras and evidence software are used by many U.S. police departments.
things_to_know: TASER devices are weapons, and police technology raises civil-liberties debates.

missions.evidence: Axon's business is public safety technology.
missions.why_line: Its cameras and software aim to make policing safer and more accountable.

profile.description: Axon makes TASER devices, body cameras and cloud software used by police and public safety agencies.
